020.idoTitle: Washing machine · explain an embedded system
o: Define an embedded system and recognise examples in everyday devices.
Describe key characteristics of embedded systems using OCR J277 language.
Explain a device's purpose, input, processing and output in an exam answer.
r: Name the three CPU characteristics that can affect performance.
Clock speed, cache size and number of CPU cores.
What does the Memory Address Register (MAR) store? What does the Program Counter (PC) store?
MAR: the address of a memory location being accessed. PC: the address of the next instruction to fetch.
What is one difference between ROM and RAM?
ROM is non-volatile and typically stores firmware; RAM is volatile and stores currently used programs and data.
A 40 × 20 bitmap uses a 4-bit colour depth. Calculate its uncompressed pixel-data size in bytes. Why would lossless compression be needed for an editable source-code file?
40 × 20 = 800 pixels; × 4 = 3,200 bits; ÷ 8 = 400 bytes. Lossless compression allows the original source code to be restored exactly.
c: An embedded system is a computer built into a larger device to perform a specific function. Unlike a general-purpose PC, it is designed for a particular job, such as controlling an automatic device.
A sensor or switch provides an input. The embedded processor follows stored instructions to make a decision, then controls an output. The output might be a display, motor, light or heater.
The dedicated control program is commonly stored in non-volatile memory (such as ROM/flash) so it remains available when power is off. RAM holds temporary data while the system runs.

Embedded systems often have limited user interfaces and are designed to use little power. Some must respond within a fixed time (real-time operation), for example where a delay would affect safety. Not every device has every feature.

m.title: Washing machine · explain an embedded system
m.q: A washing machine uses a processor to control its wash cycle. Explain why it is an embedded system, identify a sensor input, and name an output. [4 marks]
headings: Find the output and check marks
st: Identify the machine's job: controlling the washing cycle. The controller is part of a larger washing machine, not a general-purpose computer.
It is a computer built into another device [1] designed for the specific job of controlling the wash cycle [1].
A water-level sensor sends information to the controller [1]. Other relevant sensors could include temperature sensors.
The controller may switch the drum motor on/off as an output [1]. Total: 4 clear marking points — larger device, dedicated purpose, input, output.

w: A thermostat keeps a classroom warm. Explain why its controller is an embedded system. Name one input and one output. [4 marks]

It is a computer built into a larger thermostat/heating-control device [1] for a dedicated temperature-control function [1]. A temperature sensor provides the input [1]; the controller switches the heating on or off as an output [1].
A pedestrian crossing uses a push button and signal lights. Explain why its controller is an embedded system, giving an input and an output. [4 marks]

The controller is built into the crossing system [1] and has the dedicated function of controlling the signals [1]. The push button provides an input [1]; the red/green pedestrian lights are an output [1].
A fitness tracker runs from a small battery and has only a tiny display. Explain why low power and a limited user interface are appropriate. [4 marks]

Low power consumption [1] allows longer operation between charges [1]. A limited interface [1] is enough to display brief readings and reduces size/complexity for a device with a specific purpose [1].
wSteps: Your turn · identify the job
Think: what does the thermostat do? Identify a sensor and an output before writing your four-mark answer.
Step 1 · identify the device
The thermostat is part of a larger heating-control system. Its dedicated task is to monitor and control temperature.
Step 2 · explain why it is embedded
It is a computer built into another device [1], designed for a specific function rather than many general-purpose jobs [1].
Step 3 · show input and output
The temperature sensor supplies an input [1]. The controller switches the heating on or off [1].
Step 4 · check the four marks
Check four distinct points: built into a device [1]; dedicated job [1]; input sensor [1]; output/action [1].
Your turn · plan four points
Look at the pedestrian crossing. What dedicated job does it perform, and what are its input and output?
Step 1 · identify its purpose
The computer is part of the crossing equipment [1] and controls its signals for a particular task [1].
Step 2 · trace the input/output
Push button = input [1]. Red/green lights = output [1]. The controller follows instructions to operate the signals.
Step 3 · check the answer
Give four clear points, not four examples of outputs. Follow the same device → job → input → output method used in I Do.
Your turn · identify two characteristics
A tracker must work for long periods and has a small screen. Choose the two relevant characteristics.
Step 1 · explain low power
Low power consumption [1] means the tracker can operate for longer using its limited battery [1].
Step 2 · explain the interface
A limited user interface [1] is sufficient for displaying a few readings and making basic selections [1].
Step 3 · check four marks
Two linked explanations: characteristic and reason (2 + 2 marks). Avoid claiming that all embedded systems must have tiny displays.

k.q: Code First · predict how a classroom greenhouse ventilation controller responds to a temperature reading. Use OCR Exam Reference Language.
k.code:
temperature = 29
if temperature > 28 then
    print("Ventilation on")
else
    print("Ventilation off")
endif
p: Predict the exact output for temperature = 29 and explain which condition is tested.
Change the temperature to 22 and predict the output before running it.
Extend by adding limit = 28. Replace the number in the IF statement with the variable limit. Test at temperature = 28, explaining whether ventilation starts.
k.a:
Original output: Ventilation on (29 is greater than 28).

With temperature = 22, the output is: Ventilation off.

Complete extended OCR ERL solution:
temperature = 28
limit = 28
if temperature > limit then
    print("Ventilation on")
else
    print("Ventilation off")
endif

Expected output at 28: Ventilation off. The condition is strictly greater than, so equality does not switch the ventilation on.

The values simulate a reading; no physical sensor or actual greenhouse is connected.

e:
State TWO characteristics of an embedded system. [2 marks]

Source: Adapted from the Embedded Systems questions in your Paper 1 revision booklet, 1.1.3.

Designed for a specific function [1] and built into a larger device [1]. Also acceptable where relevant: a limited user interface, low power consumption, or real-time response. Credit two distinct valid characteristics.

A car-park barrier uses a vehicle sensor and a motor to lift the barrier when authorised. Explain why its controller is an embedded system, and identify an input and an output. [4 marks]

Source: Original OCR J277-style application question based on specification 1.1.3.

It is a computer built into the wider barrier system [1] for the specific function of controlling entry [1]. Input: a vehicle-detection sensor [1]. Output: controlling the motor to raise/lower the barrier [1]. 'Barrier' alone is not a specific input or output.

A battery-powered smoke alarm uses a sensor to detect smoke and activates a loud sounder when smoke is detected. Explain THREE embedded-system characteristics that make it suitable for this job. [6 marks]

Source: Original OCR J277-style applied question based on the characteristics listed in your Paper 1 revision booklet, 1.1.3.

Dedicated purpose [1]: designed specifically to detect smoke and raise an alarm [1]. Low power [1]: helps the device run for a long time from its battery [1]. Real-time response [1]: detects smoke and triggers the sounder within the required time, reducing dangerous delay [1]. Alternatives may earn credit if they correctly explain a relevant characteristic, such as non-volatile program storage. Model mark points for original practice, not an official OCR mark scheme.
v: A computer built into a larger device to perform a specific function.
A particular task for which a system has been designed.
An input device that detects or measures a physical condition.
An output device that produces a physical action, such as switching or moving a mechanism.
A system responds to inputs within a required time limit.
Memory that keeps stored information even when power is switched off.
The controls or display through which a person interacts with a system.
x: Every embedded system must have a full keyboard and monitor.
